sets.name: Domestic Injuries
sets.description: Burns, insect bites and stings, and animal bites, with their types, signs, first aid management, and prevention.

terms.definition: Physical harm from intentional violence, abuse, or accidental mishap occurring within the home.
Damage to skin or deeper tissue caused by heat, electricity, chemicals, radiation, or friction.
Outer skin only; red and painful.
Outer and second layer; blisters develop.
All skin layers destroyed; may appear white, black, or charred; nerve damage may mean no pain is felt.

Cool under cool running water for at least 20 minutes; remove jewelry and tight clothing before swelling; cover with a clean, non-stick dressing. Do not apply toothpaste, butter, oil, or ice directly. Seek immediate medical attention for severe burns.
An insect bites or injects venom into the skin; usually mild, but may trigger anaphylaxis.

Signs: pain, redness, swelling, itching, and a small raised bump. First aid: move away from the insect, wash the area with soap and clean water, scrape a bee stinger off without squeezing, apply a cold compress for 10 to 20 minutes, do not scratch, and monitor for worsening symptoms.

Anaphylaxis signs: difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, rapid pulse, dizziness, and loss of consciousness. First aid: call emergency services immediately, assist with an epinephrine auto-injector if prescribed and trained, and keep the person calm while monitoring breathing until help arrives.
Animals break the skin with their teeth; risks include bleeding, infection, rabies, and tetanus.

Ensure safety and move away from the animal; wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes; allow it to bleed slightly unless severe; apply antiseptic such as povidone-iodine if available; cover with a clean, sterile dressing; and seek medical attention immediately. Do not apply a tourniquet, suck the wound, use home remedies, or ignore small bites.
Observe a biting domestic animal for 14 days; complete the full course of anti-rabies shots.
Wear long sleeves and pants, use repellent, remove standing water, and avoid nests.
Do not provoke animals, avoid strays, supervise children, vaccinate pets, and report aggressive animals.
